Oil in a non-polar, meaning it has a neutral charge. Ethanol has polar and non-polar aspects, meaning the non-polar parts will be able to dissolve the oil. Like dissolves like!

If you'd like to remove the ethanol and are going for pure cannabis oil extract (for dabbing), my favorite method is rapid air exchange. Simply pour the liquid into a deep dish, cover with a nylon sock to prevent any dust and take a pretty good fan to blow over the whole mess for a while. An hour or two and you should get a good majority of the ethanol off. This can be done at room temperature to avoid any heat source which may cause ignition. Plus, IMO, the less heat used during processing, the better.

If you do want to use heat, I suggest a double boiler/baine marie, and a really good laser thermometer. Alcohol will boil off at around 174 F, while most of the oil will boil off at a higher temperature. You will lose some of the more volatile chemicals like terpines and some of the flavor, but the result will still pack a punch. Also do this under a hood to prevent any mishaps.

Cleanup: Isopropyl alcohol works great. I prefer olive oil though to loosen up any really stuck oil messes, then Bon Ami and soap.

4m:45s "We're not trying to strip the chlorophyll out of the plant, just the active cannabinoids."

4m:56s " I suggest squeezing it until nothing is left"

These two statements are contradictory. If you want nice clean yellow oil for smoking, have your everclear in the freezer and dump it cold onto the bud. Don't be afraid to use too much, the bud should be drowning in alcohol. I recommend pyrex glass or similar (boro-silicate) I wouldn't use aluminum like this guy as it is a toxic metal that reacts with alcohol, and definitely do not use crystalware / lead crystal as it is a very good way to give yourself lead poisoning.

Anyways, you don't want your bud in the alcohol for very long, 30 seconds to a minute is lots. Then strain it through a sieve, set the bud aside and pour the liquid straight into a coffee filter. You can use a natural unbleached one if you are afraid of the chemicals from the paper making process. Do not squeeze. I repeat, do not squeeze. Let the filter drain naturally, it will take some time. Once it is all drained use another cold flush of alcohol to get any remaining potency out of whatever's caught in the filter.

Once you've finished filtering, set the container aside. You do not need to heat it if you plan on smoking it, and you don't need to heat it at all for it to evaporate. Put it away someplace safe and let it evaporate on its own, it should take a few days.

Next, what you have left for bud still has some potency left in it but it will be mixed up with some other stuff you might not want like chlorophyll. Soak the rest of the remaining bud in alcohol and put in a covered container in the freezer, you can let it sit for 24-48 hours. the more alcohol the better.

Once the soaking is complete repeat the process. This next batch will have some darker colour to it, but still quite potent. If you really want you can try to squeeze some last bit out of the bud that remains, but likely you won't get anything useful.

If you do plan on taking any of the aforementioned products internally you will need to decarboxylate by adding heat. This is the semi-dangerous part as alcohol vapours are highly flammable (duh). I suggest using a hot-plate, even a cheap one as long as it has an adjustable temperature with readout. Lots of people say it has to reach a certain temperature to activate, but the truth is a lower temperature for a longer period works just as well. The temp readout likely won't be accurate but don't worry about it, just keep it below the boiling point and let it simmer for a couple hours, it will be fine. It should change colour slightly to become a little more brown.

If you want to get your residue off the bottom of the container and into something smaller, you can use a little bit of grain alcohol once again, and / or gently heat the bottom of the container until it starts to flow. Patience is a virtue.
